summary: Excellent, technically sound mission design report for ZYZZsat. All required elements are addressed with verified hand calculations, STK evidence and proper referencing. To reach the very top of the rubric, add an elevation-constrained access analysis, an X-band link budget, and a solar-cycle-aware decay analysis.
next_steps: Re-run STK access analysis with a 10° elevation constraint and report usable pass durations instead of approximating them from unconstrained accesses.
Add an X-band link budget (EIRP, path loss, data rate, margin) to Section 2.4 to close the acknowledged gap.
Refine the Section 2.5 decay analysis by propagating across solar-cycle density variation rather than a single mean density, and update the Vega C flight record comparison for a 2025 launch.
Tighten vague references (e.g. [15]) so every citation is specific and traceable.
Slightly deepen the Introduction's rationale/funding discussion and expand the Conclusion beyond its current brevity.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your Introduction covers all requirements: primary mission (5 m imaging of the Great Barrier Reef), rationale with cited context, single-spacecraft justification, and operator/customers (AIMS). Next level needs slightly more depth on rationale and funding context, with fuller referencing of the mission-need discussion.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Your launch (Vega C rideshare from Kourou), orbit design (verified J2 sun-sync hand calculation, i = 97.79°), manoeuvres, ground control, access frequency, duration and EOL are all well supported by STK screenshots, tables and hand calculations. To reach the top band, add the missing X-band link budget and re-run accesses with an elevation constraint.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (8/10). Your conclusions follow directly from the evidence and honestly identify four limitations and further work. They are specific and useful, but brief; expanding each conclusion with quantitative support would lift this criterion further.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (9/10). Your report has clear structure, an executive summary, labelled figures/tables, consistent IEEE-style citations matching the bibliography, and good grammar. Minor improvement: make references like [15] more specific, and keep formatting consistency throughout.
